correctness.rationale: For λ>0, Q homogeneous of odd degree 2p+1, f(θ)=⟨u,Q(u)⟩<0 and sign-definite g(θ)=⟨Ju,Q(u)⟩≠0, positive radial solutions are globally forward bounded and cannot touch r=0. With oriented s=sgn(g)θ and v=r^(2p), dv/ds=(2p f/|g|)v+2pλ/|g|. The integrating factor yields exact P(v)=ρv+B, 0<ρ<1 and B>0. Thus unique fixed positive graph and all-turn contraction, no other nonzero periodic orbit. Integrating dlog r/ds over the graph gives λT=−∫ f/|g| dθ in original physical time, and logρ=−2pλT; the transverse Poincaré derivative is ρ and tangential multiplier 1. Cubic Q=−[a r²+ε(x²−y²)]z+ωr²Jz (a>|ε|, ω>0) has f=−a−εcos2θ, g=ω, yielding T=2πa/(λω), ρ=exp(−4πa/ω), noncircular for ε≠0. Analytic generality is independent of the finite RK4 illustrative check.
residual_risks: Strict f<0 and g≠0 are essential; no assertion for angular zeros/polycycles, nonhomogeneous perturbations or backward time. The same ratio holds per revolution, not per equal physical-time interval off-cycle.
